gate.note: val MAE 0.90 is between 0.8 and 1.0. Report to Larry/Didier for decision.

observations: Split imbalance: conservative group-split produced 60.7% train / 7.7% val / 31.6% test (4 archetypes x 60 scene keys -> stricter split wins -> large test set).

Label distribution is negatively skewed (mean=-1.27) -- designer modifier table v0.5 favors negative deltas. Neutral-positive buckets [0,+5) have higher MAE (1.6-1.8) than extreme negatives [-5,-4) (0.29). Model predicts extreme negatives well but struggles on positive territory.
No gradient explosion or NaN observed. Grad norm stayed under 10 throughout.
Early stopping did not trigger (patience=10, MAE kept improving slowly to epoch 48).
Train loss decreased monotonically: 1.83 -> 0.63 -> 0.51. Healthy convergence.
R^2=0.79 on test -- model explains ~79% of label variance, which is strong for a first run on synthetic data.
Encoder cache: 149961 unique prose strings encoded in ~107s on RTX A2000 CUDA fp16.
Root cause of YELLOW gate: val set too small (3835 samples) due to group-split imbalance; MAE estimate noisy. Real val set (Varn hand-graded) may differ significantly.
recommendation: Report to Larry/Didier. Given R2=0.79 and train-loss convergence, the model is learning. The YELLOW is dominated by val-set size (3835 samples from 2 archetypes / ~6 scenes). Two paths: (A) adjust split to guarantee a larger val share before re-running; (B) accept YELLOW for M1 synthetic baseline and use the 200-500 Varn hand-graded set (substep 10 gate criterion) as the definitive MAE signal.
